body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application.

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A physical therapy or palpation glove device, the glove device comprising:
a glove. comprising. at least one layer of material;
one or more pressure sensors secured to and located adiacent to a side edge of the glove, the one or more pressure sensors configured for detecting pressure applied by a user's hand wearing the glove onto a vertebra or soft tissue of an individual, and
a microcontroller secured to and located on the glove, the microcontroller electrically connected to the one or more pressure sensors, the microcontroller receiving electrical signal inputs from the one or more sensors and generating an output signal.
2. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein the one or more pressure sensors is multiple pressure sensors secured to the glove.
3. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 2, wherein the multiple pressure sensors are spaced apart on the glove.
4. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein one of the one or more pressure sensors is located in a thumb portion of the glove.
5. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein one of the one or more pressure sensors is located in a finger portion of the glove.
6. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 2, wherein one of the one or more pressure sensors is located on a back of the glove.
7. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein one of the one or more pressure sensors comprises multiple pressure sensors located on the side of the glove.
8. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein the [[the]] at least one layer is an inner liner and exterior layer.
9. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 8, wherein the one or more pressure sensors and microcontroller are secured located between the exterior layer and inner liner of the glove.
10. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein the one or more pressure sensors is one selected from the group consisting of a force measuring capacitor, a force-sensitive resistor, and a tactile pressure sensor.
11. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein the one or more pressure sensors comprises a first sensor positioned to detect pressure applied by a thumb of the user and a second sensor positioned to detect pressure applied by a side of an index finger of the user.
12. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 11, wherein the one or more pressure sensors further comprises a third sensor positioned to detect pressure applied by a back of [[a]] the hand of the user.
13. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 12, wherein the one or more pressure sensor sensors comprises a fourth sensor and a fifth sensor positioned to detect pressure applied by a side of the hand of the user.
14. (Currently Amended) A glove system comprising a computer electrically connected to the glove device according to claim 1, [[and]] the computer configured for receiving the output signal from the microcontroller of the glove device during operation of the glove system.
15. (Currently Amended) The glove system according to claim 14, wherein the computer is located remote remotely relative to the glove device.
16. (Withdrawn) A palpation evaluation or diagnosis system, the system comprising:
a physical therapy or palpation glove device comprising one or more pressure sensors located on a side of the device and connected to a microprocessor;
an individual pain indicator device; and
a computer for receiving an output signal from the microprocessor of the physical therapy glove and an output signal from the patient pain indicator device.
17. (Currently Amended, Withdrawn) The system according to claim 16, wherein the physical therapy glove is one according to claim 1 comprises:
at least one layer of material;
wherein the one or more pressure sensors are secured to and located adiacent to a side edge of the glove, the one or more pressure sensors configured for detecting pressure applied by a user's hand wearing the glove onto a vertebra or soft tissue of an individual; and
a microcontroller secured to and located on the glove, the microcontroller electrically connected to the one or more pressure sensors, the microcontroller receiving electrical signal inputs from the one or more sensors and generating an output signal.
18. (Withdrawn) The system according to claim 16, wherein the computer is programmed to compute a pain force index using the output signal transmitted from the physical therapy or palpation glove device to the computer corresponding to a minimum pressure applied by the user wearing the glove to a vertebra of an individual and the output signal transmitted from the individual pain indicator device to the computer corresponding to pain intensity.
19. (Currently Amended, Withdrawn) The system according to claim 16, wherein the [[the]] pain force index is determined using a formula of 10 - painLevel + minForce.
20. (Withdrawn) A spine palpation evaluation or diagnosis method, the method comprising:
detecting a force applied to a patient's vertebra by a glove device comprising one or more sensors located on a side of the glove device;
detecting a level of pain by a patient; and
evaluating progress in a treatment of a particular vertebrae and/or soft tissue of the patient.
21. (Currently Amended, Withdrawn) The method according to claim 20, further comprising capturing pain or discomfort in real-time from an individual using [[a]] an individual pain indicator device for logging in the pressure when pain is encountered by the patient individual while being medically treated for a problem.
22. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 2, wherein the multiple pressure sensors comprises a thumb pressure sensor and a side index finger pressure sensor.
23. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 22, wherein the multiple pressure sensors further comprise one or more side hand pressure sensors.
24. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 23, wherein the one or more side hand pressure sensors are two side-by-side hand pressure sensors.
25. (Previously Presented) The glove device according to claim 24, further comprising a pressure sensor located on a back of the glove.
26. (Currently Amended) The glove device according to claim 1, wherein the glove is configured to accommodate [[only]] a thumb and extended index finger.
27. (Currently Amended) A physical therapy or palpation glove device, the glove device comprising:
a glove. comprising at least one layer of material;
one or more pressure sensors secured to and located on a back side of the glove, the one or more pressure sensors configured for detecting pressure applied by a user's hand wearing the glove to a vertebra or soft tissue of an individual, and
a microcontroller secured to located on the glove, the microcontroller
electrically connected to the one or more pressure sensors, the microcontroller receiving electrical signal inputs from the one or more sensors and generating an output signal.
28. (New) A physical therapy or palpation glove device, the glove device comprising:
a glove, comprising:
an outer fabric glove;
an inner fabric glove located inside the outer fabric glove;
one or more pressure sensors located between the outer fabric glove and the inner fabric glove, the one or more pressure sensors configured for detecting pressure applied by a user's hand wearing the glove onto a vertebra or soft tissue of an individual, and
a microcontroller located between the outer fabric glove and the inner fabric glove, the microcontroller electrically connected to the one or more pressure sensors, the microcontroller receiving electrical signal inputs from the one or more sensors and generating an output signal.
29. (New) The device according to claim 28, wherein outer perimeter edges of the outer fabric glove and inner fabric glove are sewn together 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
